question: Which finite-matrix twist-gauge convention should replace the incompatible combination of [0,1) twist reduction, bare site-permutation D4 covariance, and the generic twist (0.37,-0.23) in the accepted Stage B design?

options.summary: Use the centred twist representative and a uniform-link gauge.
options.consequence: Represent twists in [-1/2,1/2), so every D4 image of the frozen generic twist remains in the same centred domain; construct the finite Hamiltonian in the uniform-link gauge and retain the bare permutation U_M in the covariance equations. The prior [0,1) reduction requirement is replaced.

options.summary: Keep [0,1) twist reduction and use a twist-dependent covariance unitary.
options.consequence: Use a periodic seam-compatible finite representation and replace bare full-Hamiltonian covariance by a gauge-decorated symmetry W_M(phi); retain the bare permutation only for the twist-independent onsite defect. The verifier must independently reconstruct W_M(phi).

options.summary: Retain reduced metadata plus an explicit unreduced twist lift.
options.consequence: Construct and compare matrices in a uniform-link gauge using the unreduced lift M*phi, retain M*phi modulo one as boundary-fibre metadata, and record the integer lift and its gauge relation explicitly. Bare-permutation covariance applies only to lifted matrices.

options.summary: Do not revise or implement Stage B.
options.consequence: Retain the design-level incompatibility and partial execution-free implementation as a negative development finding; no Stage B execution request is made.

options.summary: Adopt two independent matrix routes, one explicit gauge bridge, both route orders, and data-complete retention; authorize execution-free implementation only.
options.consequence: Replace the incompatible single-route convention with the reviewed centered-uniform and reduced-seam constructors, explicit lift/gauge bridge, A-then-B and B-then-A schedules, complete route/candidate/adverse/order retention, runner, independent verifier, schemas, plotting, and authored toy behavioral tests. Accepted-parent execution remains unauthorized.

recommendation: ADOPT_MULTIROUTE_DATA_COMPLETE_EXECUTION_FREE_IMPLEMENTATION. It preserves the most route, gauge, order, ambiguity, adverse-control, and provenance information for later data-based evaluation while retaining route disagreement and order sensitivity as failures rather than selecting a favorable result.
safe_scope: Adopt and implement the exact execution-free multi-route design: runner, independent verifier, data-complete schemas, deterministic plotting from retained toy/result records, and authored toy behavioral tests. Do not read or execute the accepted scalar parent and do not create stage-b-result.json.
blocked_scope: Stage B execution with the accepted parent, creation or interpretation of an accepted-parent Stage B result, Stage C through E, prerequisite reruns, DFT, Wannier90, materials, scientific validation, uncertainty quantification, publication, release, deposit, and external transmission remain unauthorized.
authorized_scope: Adopt the exact proposed two-route, one-bridge, two-schedule data-complete Stage B replacement and implement only its fail-closed runner, independent verifier, closed retained-data schemas, deterministic plotting from retained records, and authored toy-coefficient behavioral tests. Preserve all route-local, cross-route, cross-schedule, blind-candidate, adverse-control, stop, resource, and provenance data within the declared bounds. Do not read or execute the accepted scalar parent and do not create an accepted-parent Stage B result.
